narrative.overview:
This is a 1990s operating system shell running on modern React, fully aware of what it is. The portfolio does not simulate Windows 95 as a novelty trick — it commits to the metaphor completely: draggable windows, a functioning taskbar, a boot sequence, a BSOD, Minesweeper, Snake. The visitor is not looking at a portfolio with a retro skin. They are using a machine.

The design system is built from the bevel. Every surface — buttons, windows, inputs, cards, the taskbar — uses the same four-layer double-border technique that Win95 used. Elevation is theatrical, not ambient: shadows exist because they are part of the performance. Typography follows a strict split: IBM Plex Mono for anything that belongs to the OS and IBM Plex Sans for anything that is human-facing content. One font family, two registers, complete discipline.
keyCharacteristics: Bevel-based elevation — four-layer double-border + inset shadow for every raised or sunken surface
Zero border radius — all OS chrome is pixel-sharp
Two-font discipline — Mono for the system, Sans for the person
Sky blue desktop gradient as the primary environment
Theatrical motion — animation is part of the OS illusion

rules.name: The One Focus Rule
rules.body: Active Window Blue (#000080 to #1084d0) appears in exactly one place: the window titlebar gradient. Its power comes from its exclusivity.

rules.name: The No-Pure-Extreme Rule
rules.body: No pure #000000 or #ffffff in any surface or text role. Every neutral is tinted.

rules.name: The System/Human Split Rule
rules.body: IBM Plex Mono is the OS speaking. IBM Plex Sans is the person. Any new element that belongs to OS chrome uses Mono. Any element that is content uses Sans. No exceptions.

rules.name: The Bevel-Only Rule
rules.body: All elevation is expressed through the bevel system. Do not add blurred box-shadow values to new OS-chrome components.

dos: Do use the bevel system for all new components with raised or pressed states.
Do use IBM Plex Mono for OS chrome and IBM Plex Sans for human-facing content.
Do keep all OS chrome at 0px border-radius.
Do use Active Window Blue exclusively on window titlebars and system focus rings.
Do include prefers-reduced-motion overrides for any new animation.
Do ask whether a new feature fits as a window, desktop icon, taskbar item, or dialog before inventing a new pattern.
Do animate with transform and opacity only, using ease-out-expo curves.
donts: Don't add border-radius to OS chrome components.
Don't add blurred box-shadow values to new components.
Don't ship a generic dark-mode portfolio with hero sections and glowing stack badges.
Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text + gradient background).
Don't use Active Window Blue as a decorative accent outside titlebars and focus rings.
Don't add a border-left or border-right stripe larger than 1px as a colored accent.
Don't animate layout properties — transform and opacity only.
Don't use bounce or elastic easing.
Don't add content that reads as AI-assembled with no specific context.
